input.command:
T_SID='ACb44cb1d853b03144f7799d5eea09f63a'
T_TOKEN='9e28af71d4a5b5a1219f6b7a37e1c367'
FROM_PHONE='+15617822411'
TO_PHONE='+15616443503'

echo "=== Test new token #6 ==="
AUTH_HTTP=$(curl -s -o /tmp/tw_acct.json -w '%{http_code}' \
  -u "$T_SID:$T_TOKEN" \
  "https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01/Accounts/$T_SID.json")
echo "HTTP: $AUTH_HTTP"

if [ "$AUTH_HTTP" = "200" ]; then
  echo "AUTH VERIFIED!"
  python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('/tmp/tw_acct.json')); print(f'Account: {d.get(\"friendly_name\",\"?\")} Status: {d.get(\"status\",\"?\")}')"
  rm -f /tmp/tw_acct.json

  echo ""
  echo "=== Sending SMS to $TO_PHONE from $FROM_PHONE ==="
  SMS_RESULT=$(curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}' -u "$T_SID:$T_TOKEN" \
    -X POST \
    --data-urlencode "To=$TO_PHONE" \
    --data-urlencode "From=$FROM_PHONE" \
    --data-urlencode "Body=IVX AI Verification: Autonomous work report SMS system is LIVE. Twilio integration confirmed end-to-end. $(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
    "https://api.twilio.com/2010-04-01/Accounts/$T_SID/Messages.json")
  SMS_HTTP=$(echo "$SMS_RESULT" | tail -1)
  SMS_BODY=$(echo "$SMS_RESULT" | head -n -1)
  echo "HTTP: $SMS_HTTP"
  echo "$SMS_BODY" | python3 -m json.tool 2>/dev/null || echo "$SMS_BODY" | head -c 800
else
  echo "AUTH FAILED"
  cat /tmp/tw_acct.json
  rm -f /tmp/tw_acct.json
fi

2. The Account SID or the account itself is the real problem

Let me check if the Account SID is actually the one associated with a live Twilio account, by trying to see if a completely wrong token gets the same error as any token:

I already ran the fake-SID comparison and it returned the same 401. So Twilio gives 401 for both invalid tokens and invalid SIDs. That doesn't help distinguish.

Let me try to inspect the Twilio account's public side — check if the account SID appears in any of your Twilio-owned assets, or try the Twilio Lookup API to see if the number `+15617822411` belongs to that account:

Alternatively, I can try to help you use the Twilio CLI to generate a valid token, but that also requires login.

Let me think about the actual code bug. The user is frustrated and thinks I'm the issue. The honest issue is that Twilio rotated tokens. But maybe the Rork platform is also caching an old token, or the env var update didn't propagate.

2. Ask the user to log in to Twilio Console right now and take a screenshot of the LIVE CREDENTIALS page (or paste the exact token)
